lead.headline: White House Crypto Meeting Signals CFTC Ascendancy Over SEC in Regulatory Turf War
lead.tldr: Trump hosting crypto executives alongside CFTC Chair Selig—while the CLARITY Act stalls—suggests the administration is betting on commodities regulators over securities enforcers, with prediction markets now bundled into the same political package.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, today's brief tracks how regulatory momentum is concentrating in one agency's corner while tokenized equities quietly scale to $23 billion monthly volume—two developments that reshape how we underwrite compliance risk and secondary-market liquidity.

top_signals.title: Trump, CFTC Chair Selig expected at Wednesday White House meeting with crypto and prediction market executives
top_signals.summary: President Trump and CFTC Chair Rusty Selig are expected to meet with crypto and prediction market executives at the White House this Wednesday. The meeting serves as a kickoff for the CFTC's inaugural Innovation Advisory Committee meeting.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The White House optics—Trump plus Selig, not Gensler—are a directional bet on CFTC jurisdiction that reprices every US exchange and DeFi protocol's legal roadmap, especially with prediction markets now explicitly in the room.

top_signals.title: ‘The great quantum migration’ is coming as more than $2 trillion in digital assets is at risk—nearly the entire value of the overall crypto market
top_signals.summary: The crypto market faces a systemic risk as quantum computing threatens the elliptic-curve cryptography securing over $2 trillion in digital assets. Quantus CEO Christoper Smith warns of a necessary 'great quantum migration' to protect the industry from future quantum attacks.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Quantum risk to $2 trillion in cryptographic-secured assets is an unpriced tail risk in most token valuations and infrastructure due diligence, one that will eventually force costly migration of legacy UTXO and account-based systems.

top_signals.title: Israel’s largest bank taps Galaxy to offer Bitcoin, Ether, Solana trading10m
top_signals.summary: Israel's largest bank has partnered with Galaxy to enable the trading of major digital assets including Bitcoin, Ether, and Solana. This move signals significant institutional adoption of cryptocurrencies within the Israeli banking sector.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Israel's largest bank outsourcing to Galaxy rather than building proprietary stacks validates the B2B infrastructure thesis and narrows the competitive set for regulated crypto custody and execution in G20 banking.

top_signals.title: Binance to restrict transactions involving HTX, 10 other crypto platforms11m
top_signals.summary: Binance is implementing restrictions on transactions involving HTX and ten other cryptocurrency platforms. This move is likely aimed at enhancing security and compliance measures regarding fund transfers between exchanges.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Binance's platform-level transaction restrictions signal intensifying exchange self-regulation that fragments liquidity pools and raises counterparty diligence costs for trading strategies across venues.

top_signals.title: Tokenized stock holders more than double as monthly volume surges
top_signals.summary: The number of tokenized stock holders has more than doubled over the last month, reaching 1.31 million. Monthly transfer volume for these assets also saw a significant surge, climbing to $23.13 billion.
top_signals.why_it_matters: 1.31 million tokenized stock holders and $23.13 billion monthly transfer volume demonstrate that tokenized securities have crossed from proof-of-concept to scalable distribution, though legal finality of ownership remains jurisdictionally untested.

on_the_radar.title: Kalshi ordered to stop broad range of prediction markets in Washington38m, Kalshi ordered to stop broad range of prediction markets in WashingtonKalshi must implement initial geofencing by Aug. 19 and a GeoComply multi-source geofencing system by Sept. 2.
on_the_radar.summary: Kalshi has been ordered to halt a broad range of its prediction markets within the state of Washington. The company is required to implement strict geofencing measures by August 19 and September 2 to ensure compliance.

on_the_radar.title: 'Honestly, I don't care': Tether CEO dismisses critics following first KPMG audit
on_the_radar.summary: Tether's CEO has dismissed critics regarding the company's transparency following its first audit by KPMG. The company maintains that it does not publicly share audited statements because it operates as a private entity.

on_the_radar.title: Fizzling CLARITY Act Odds Leave SEC and CFTC Scrambling to Act
on_the_radar.summary: The likelihood of the CLARITY Act passing in 2026 is decreasing, leaving the SEC and CFTC to navigate regulatory gaps. The SEC reportedly considered offering major exemptions to foster crypto innovation but has since backtracked.

on_the_radar.title: Shinhan Asset Management partners with Plume on tokenized fund pilot
on_the_radar.summary: Shinhan Asset Management is partnering with Plume to launch a pilot for a tokenized fund. The project will focus on a Korean won-denominated fund backed by ultra-short-term bonds.

on_the_radar.title: Strategy, Metaplanet could face MSCI index removal under new proposal
on_the_radar.summary: MSCI is proposing a new non-operating company screen that could lead to the removal of MicroStrategy and Metaplanet from its global indexes. This move targets companies whose primary activity is holding assets rather than traditional operations.

on_the_radar.title: RedotPay US IPO delayed amid regulatory, legal hurdles: Report
on_the_radar.summary: RedotPay's planned US IPO has been delayed due to regulatory hurdles and legal challenges. The company is currently facing a lawsuit from Binance affiliates totaling nearly $473 million.

on_the_radar.title: JPMorgan cut Polymarket banking ties over regulatory concerns: Report29m
on_the_radar.summary: JPMorgan has reportedly severed its banking relationship with the prediction market Polymarket due to regulatory concerns. This move highlights the ongoing tension between traditional financial institutions and decentralized betting platforms.

on_the_radar.title: French tax breach exposes nearly 678,000 people as crypto wrench attacks pile up
on_the_radar.summary: A data breach of French tax records has exposed the personal information of nearly 678,000 individuals, potentially increasing the risk of targeted attacks. This occurs amidst a rising trend of 'wrench attacks'—violent crimes targeting cryptocurrency holders in France.

linkedin_post: The CFTC's Innovation Advisory Committee is meeting at the White House this Wednesday. Trump will be there. So will Rusty Selig. The SEC chair will not. That is not an oversight. The CLARITY Act—designed to settle the SEC-CFTC turf war—is fizzling in Congress, which means the agencies are scrambling to act unilaterally. The White House just placed its chip on Selig's side of the table. For founders building in the US, this matters because the CFTC's framework for commodities and, increasingly, prediction markets, is narrower and more permissive than the SEC's securities-based enforcement machine. We are underwriting US regulatory risk on the assumption that the CFTC's remit expands through administrative action where legislation fails. The test: whether the CFTC publishes a workable registration pathway for prediction market operators before the SEC issues a no-action letter for tokenized equities. One of those will happen first. The other may not happen at all. Tokenized stocks are scaling regardless—$23 billion in monthly volume, 1.31 million holders. The market is moving faster than either agency's rulebook. Our question is which regulator catches up, and which gets bypassed.
